title: Hyperion docs, redesigned for 4.5
question: Compare three structures in the Hyperion and Rio Blocks visual system. These are first-viewport sketches, not an implemented docs site. The full content and migration proposal is in planning/4.5-docs-redesign/proposal.md.

options.label: The Hyperion handbook
options.thesis: One coherent reference with a persistent section rail, a calm reading column and an immediate way to start.
options.viewport: The docs shell is already open: section rail on the left, an introduction and task list in the center, local contents on the right.
options.risk: The full navigation is visible before a new reader has chosen a task.

options.label: Start with a task
options.thesis: A compact front door gives API developers, operators and plugin authors a direct route to working guidance.
options.viewport: Task routes share the first viewport with a bounded history-query example; the full sidebar begins inside the chosen section.
options.risk: The homepage adds one navigation step for readers who already know their destination.

options.label: The 4.5 release workspace
options.thesis: A release-focused front page puts readiness, upgrade guidance and existing API docs side by side.
options.viewport: The version and its preview status lead, then two reading tracks: integrate with Hyperion or prepare an operator upgrade.
options.risk: It needs a deliberate transition after 4.5 ships so the release does not permanently dominate discovery.
